en: The *Adhyardhaśatikā Prajñāpāramitā*, also known by other titles such as the *Naya-dvyardhaśatikā* and the *Ardhaśatikā*.
Oṃ! Homage to the Blessed Lady Prajñāpāramitā!
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Blessed One was together with the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi...
and by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara,
and by Ākāśagarbha, and by Vajramuṣṭi;
and Mañjuśrī,
who sets in motion the wheel of Dharma upon the mere arising of the thought of enlightenment.
and with the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gaganagañja, and the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvamārapramardin;

headed by these eight koṭis of Bodhisattvas, [he taught] that which is virtuous in the beginning, virtuous in the middle, and virtuous in the end, possessing the true meaning, well-phrased in syllables, and perfectly pure.

He taught the accomplishment of the purity of all phenomena: "This is the state of the purity of desire, namely, the state of a bodhisattva. This is the state of the purity of views, namely, the state of a bodhisattva. This is the state of the purity of delight, namely, the state of a bodhisattva."
This is the stage of the purification of craving, namely, the stage of the bodhisattva;
this is the stage of the purification of adornment, namely, the stage of the bodhisattva;
this is the stage of the purification of delight, namely, the stage of the bodhisattva.
This is the stage of purity of light, namely, the stage of the bodhisattva;
this is the stage of purity of physical bliss, namely, the stage of the bodhisattva;
this is the stage of purity of verbal bliss, namely, the stage of the bodhisattva.
This is the state of purity of mind, namely, the state of a bodhisattva; this is the state of purity of sound, namely, the state of a bodhisattva;
this is the state of purity of fragrance, namely, the state of a bodhisattva.
This is the stage of the purification of taste, namely, the stage of the bodhisattva;
this is the stage of the purification of touch, namely, the stage of the bodhisattva.
For what reason?
That is to say: all phenomena are pure by nature;
all phenomena are empty of intrinsic nature.
Through this emptiness of intrinsic nature, there is the purity of the perfection of wisdom.

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, again taught this method of the Perfection of Wisdom, which brings about the realization of the peaceful nature of all phenomena of all Tathāgatas: "In the realization of the equality of the vajra, there is great awakening through the firmness of the vajra;
in the realization of the equality of meaning, there is great awakening through the single meaning."
Great enlightenment is the perfect awakening to the equality of phenomena by virtue of its intrinsic purity;
great enlightenment is the perfect awakening to the equality of all things by virtue of the absence of all conceptual construction.

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Subduer of All Evil Ones, again taught the extraction of the perfection of wisdom called "The Compendium of Victory through the Equality of All Dharmas": "Through the non-proliferation of passion, there is the non-proliferation of hatred; through the non-proliferation of hatred, there is the non-proliferation of delusion; and through the non-proliferation of delusion, there is the non-proliferation of all dharmas."
One should understand that because all phenomena are without conceptual proliferation, the perfection of wisdom is without conceptual proliferation.

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Svabhāvaśuddha, again taught this method of the perfection of wisdom called the "Wisdom-Seal of Avalokiteśvara Who Contemplates the Equality of All Dharmas": "In the world, the purification of all passion conduces to the purification of hatred;
the purification of all impurities in the world conduces to the purification of hatred."
The purification of all stains in the world leads to the purification of all evils;
the purification of all phenomena in the world leads to the purification of all sentient beings;
and the purification of all knowledge in the world leads to the purification of the perfection of wisdom.

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the sovereign of the entire triple world, once again taught the method of the perfection of wisdom called the Matrix of Wisdom Arising from the Empowerment of All Tathāgatas: "The bestowing of empowerment leads to the attainment of sovereignty over the entire triple world;
the giving of wealth leads to the fulfillment of all hopes."
The gift of Dharma leads to the realization of the true nature of all phenomena;
the gift of material things leads to the attainment of happiness for body, speech, and mind.
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata who holds the fist of all Tathāgatas and has attained the wisdom-mudrās of all Tathāgatas,

once again taught the method of the perfection of wisdom called the Vajra Empowerment of the Wisdom-Mudrās of All Tathāgatas: "The grasping of the body-mudrā of all Tathāgatas conduces to the state of being a Tathāgata."
The adoption of the speech-mudrā conduces to the attainment of all dharmas;
the adoption of the mind-mudrā conduces to the attainment of all samādhis;
and the adoption of the vajra-mudrā conduces to the supreme accomplishment of Vajrasattva of all body, speech, and mind.

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata of the non-proliferation of all phenomena, again taught the method of the perfection of wisdom called the "Revolution of the Wheel of Syllables": "All phenomena are empty by virtue of the yoga of the absence of intrinsic nature;
all phenomena are signless by virtue of signlessness;
all phenomena are wishless by virtue of the yoga of wishlessness."
They are naturally luminous through the complete purity of the perfection of wisdom.

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata who is contained within the wheel of all Tathāgatas, again taught the method of the perfection of wisdom called "Entry into the Great Wheel": "Entry into the equality of the vajra leads to entry into the wheel of all Tathāgatas;
entry into the equality of meaning leads to entry into the wheel of the great bodhisattvas."
Entry into the equality of phenomena leads to entry into the wheel of all phenomena;
entry into the equality of all things leads to entry into all wheels.

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata who is the vessel for the full expansion of all rites of worship, again taught the method of the Perfection of Wisdom called "The Foremost of All Worship": "The generation of the thought of awakening is the full expansion of the rite of worship for all Tathāgatas;
the protection of the realm of all sentient beings is the full expansion of the rite of worship for all Tathāgatas;
the upholding of the true Dharma is the full expansion of the rite of worship for all Tathāgatas."
The extensive ritual for the worship of all Tathāgatas consists of the acts of writing, causing to be written, upholding, reading, reciting, meditating upon, and honoring the Prajñāpāramitā.

Then indeed, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata who is capable of disciplining all, again taught this method of the perfection of wisdom called *Jñānamuṣṭiparigraha-sarvasattvavinayajñānagarbha* (The Fistful of Wisdom that Embraces All, the Matrix of Wisdom for Disciplining All Beings): "In the equality of all beings is the equality of anger; in the disciplining of all beings is the disciplining of anger."
In the dharmatā of all sentient beings there is the dharmatā of wrath; in the vajra-nature of all sentient beings there is the vajra-nature of wrath.
For what reason?
The training of all sentient beings is awakening.
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata established in the equality of all phenomena, again taught this method of the perfection of wisdom called "The Foremost of All Phenomena":
"The nature of the perfection of wisdom is the nature of all purposes;
the nature of the perfection of wisdom is the nature of all phenomena."
It should be understood that the activity of the perfection of wisdom is the activity of all activities.

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, once again taught the method of the perfection of wisdom called "The Empowerment of All Sentient Beings": "All sentient beings are the womb of the Tathāgatas (*tathāgatagarbha*), because they possess the universal nature of the Great Bodhisattva Samantabhadra;
all sentient beings are the womb of the Vajra (*vajragarbha*), because they are consecrated as the womb of the Vajra;
all sentient beings are the womb of the Dharma (*dharmagarbha*), because they set forth all speech."
All sentient beings have karma as their womb, by virtue of the application of the agency of all sentient beings.

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata who is infinite, boundless, and inexhaustible, possessing infinite, boundless, and inexhaustible qualities, in order to empower the final conclusion of this eon, further taught this method of the perfection of wisdom called the "Vajra Empowerment of the Equality of All Phenomena": "Through the infinity of the perfection of wisdom, there is the infinity of all Tathāgatas."

Through the boundlessness of the perfection of wisdom, there is the boundlessness of all Tathāgatas; through the non-duality of the perfection of wisdom, there is the non-duality of all phenomena; through the ultimate consummation of the perfection of wisdom, there is the ultimate consummation of all phenomena.

Then the Blessed One Vairocana, who has attained the secret nature of all Tathāgatas and is free from the conceptual proliferation of all phenomena, again taught this entrance to the Perfection of Wisdom of the vajra-nature of the unfailing [vajra], called the Great Bliss Unfailing Vajra, which is supreme and without beginning, middle, or end: "The supreme accomplishment of great illness leads to the supreme accomplishment of great bliss for the great Bodhisattvas."
The supreme accomplishment of great bliss of the great bodhisattvas leads to the supreme accomplishment of the great awakening of all Tathāgatas.
The supreme accomplishment of the great awakening of all Tathāgatas of the great bodhisattvas leads to the supreme accomplishment of the crushing of all great Māras.
The supreme accomplishment of the crushing of all great Māras of the great bodhisattvas leads to the supreme accomplishment of sovereignty over the entire great triple world.

The supreme accomplishment of sovereignty over the entire great triple world leads to the supreme, ultimate, and great bliss for the sake of the welfare and happiness of all beings, and to the protection of the entire realm of sentient beings without exception or remainder, for the sake of the great Bodhisattvas.
For what reason?
As long as these excellent sages remain here within the sphere of existence, they are able to accomplish incomparable benefit for sentient beings without passing into nirvana. // 1 //
Accomplished through the empowerment of the knowledge of skillful means and the perfection of wisdom, they indeed become pure of existence through the purification of all karma. // 2 //
The discipline regarding passion and the like in the world has existed repeatedly and constantly from the very beginning of existence;
however, for the sake of purifying them, he himself came to know that discipline. // 3 //
Just as a deep red lotus is not stained by the defects of passion, so those who work for the welfare of the world are never stained by the defects of dwelling in existence. // 4 //
Purified by great passion, possessing great bliss and great wealth, having attained sovereignty over the three realms, may they firmly accomplish that purpose. //5// Thus.
The Perfection of Wisdom in One Hundred and Fifty Verses is completed.
